full_judgment:
Mr. Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury, J: This appeal by the complainant is by way of leave from the judgment and order dated 10 May, 1999 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2644 of 1999 transferring the Complaint Case No. 3342 of 1998 to the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The facts giving rise to the appeal are these. Upon dishonour of a cheque for Tk. 4,50,000/- drawn by the accused in favour of the complainant the complainant brought a case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 after due service of notice upon the accused. The case was eventually transferred by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who took cognizance of the case and transferred the same to the court of Mr. Shahidul Islam, Metropolitan Magistrate for trial. After the charge was framed and the case was fixed for hearing on 16 March 1999 the accused filed an application for transfer of the case from the court of the said Metropolitan Magistrate to some other Metropolitan Magistrate which was rejected. 

 3. The accused then approached the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka with an application for transfer of the case under Section 526B of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was also dismissed summarily. 

 4. The accused thereafter filed an application. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2644 of 1999, under Section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the High Court Division on the ground of bias. After hearing the parties the said court passed the impugned order transferring the case to the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka without accepting or rejecting the ground of transfer. 

 6. This submission appears perfectly cogent. Whenever an allegation is made against a court it is necessary to give a finding as to the truth or otherwise about it. This presupposes notice, although Section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not clearly speak of notice. In such a case the principle of audi alteram partem comes into play. We have already taken a similar view in the case of Md. Shahid Mia Vs. Liton and others, Criminal Appeal No. 24 of 1998.
